utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are very sorry about the delay this morning, because we don't have much time to lose for this case. So today we might sit a little bit longer to make up the 30 minutes we lost. Mr. Krsnik, cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, Witness, have you talked to someone since yesterday?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: May I remind you, yesterday we stopped when you mentioned a bunker that was off the road between Jablanica and Konjic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That was the bunker where Cikota lost his life, right?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You said yesterday that you were about ten metres away, or rather, you were there, you were present?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the vicinity, but I have not mentioned ten metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. You were in the vicinity. Can you give me the name of at least one or two soldiers who were with you?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked about it yesterday. I cannot give you any further names. The names of the persons I have been constantly in contact with, I have mentioned. It was two -- three or four people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yesterday, you also talked about the mosque, in Doljani, of course.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you said that explosive had been placed there, but you did not see it activated.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Again, you do not know the names of the soldiers who placed this explosive, right?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, you said that there was a house that was your base, and how far away is that mosque and which way is it from that house, north, south, east, west?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be in a position to tell you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All right. I'll try to show you a picture, and then perhaps you will be able to show us the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the Registrar if the witness could be shown Exhibit 8.9, actually, where he put in a few things for the Prosecutor. Also, could I kindly ask you to put the ELMO down a little bit so that I can see the witness better? Later, rather, when we finish with this particular bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yesterday, remember you were putting these dots in, one, two, three.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: For point 2, you said yesterday that that was where the imprisoned soldiers were. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: This little wooden shed, or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And you marked that with a number "2," right, on this particular picture?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to show you another picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher for his assistance. That is Prosecution Exhibit 8.10.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you see this picture now from a different angle?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you please clarify this for me: Where you said that there was a wooden shed, that is where there is a brook and a bridge; isn't is that right?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, approximately there where the car is standing now. There used to be this wooden thing, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise to the usher, but could you please put the picture that was previously on the ELMO back on the ELMO again, please; 8.9, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you see a car now in this picture, and number 2?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, if you look from number 2 towards the house, you can see a blue thing there, and the blue thing is a car, if you want to take the photograph in your hands and take a good look at it.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Why didn't you mark that position immediately, then? You said precisely that the wooden shed was here where the car is. Why didn't you mark it there immediately? Why did you mark it where number 2 is?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said approximately. Said approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Approximately. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am going to ask the usher to show the witness 8.8, Prosecution Exhibit 8.8.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you see where the mosque is in this picture, or the direction in which it was, up or down, left or right?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. On the right-hand side behind this direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind as to -- oh, this is a Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, can we actually ask the witness to mark things on this photograph as well? [In English] Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please be so kind as to take a marker, and could you please mark an arrow from the house in the direction which you said the mosque was.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So if we look at this direction, how far away was it from this particular building?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you. I couldn't give you this distance in metres. I really don't know. I just wanted to bear you in mind that it's eight years since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Witness, do you remember how many statements you gave? I asked you that yesterday already, but I would like to have it repeated today. How many statements did you give to the investigators and prosecutors of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you give one statement or several?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting, Mr. President. As Mr. Krsnik has just conceded, this question was asked and answered yesterday by the witness, and on that basis I would object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krsnik, is this necessary for you to ask this question again? Because we had it yesterday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I can skip it, but we have this communication problem because the witness finds it hard to remember things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you remember the statement that you gave on the 16th and 17th of April 1997?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that they were with me, but how shall I know what I have said on this particular two days?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'll remind you. If you recall, Susan Somers was present that day. It is not customary for a trial attorney from The Hague to come to prison. Do you remember now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I have two things to say, Mr. President. First, counsel doesn't know whether it's customary or not for counsel or anyone else to go see witnesses, and so I think that he's not in a position to make or to put such a statement to the witness. Secondly, I'd ask that if he intends to ask the witness about a statement that the witness gave, the witness ought to be given an opportunity to at least look at the statement to see which statement he's being asked about, to see whether he recognises the statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, you may skip this question, and if you will use this statement, it's better to show this statement to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With pleasure, Your Honour, but please may I first respond to my learned friend? Actually, I asked whether Susan Somers was present for a very specific reason and for relevant reasons. I shall shed more light on this through my following questions, because the witness had an ongoing correspondence with her, but we will get to that too. I will be very glad to make a statement, and I would be very glad to give this witness his statement, but I -- this witness speaks German, and I haven't got a German version. I don't have a Croatian version either, so that's why I thought that I should read parts of his statement Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to him, some of the things he stated there on that particular day to The Hague investigators and the Prosecutor too. But I have the Croatian version. It's not going to take very long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, so long as it's not that long. Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, maybe I misunderstood. It was my impression that the Trial Chamber had decided that the witness would be shown the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, I understand that, but the counsel said that he does not have the other versions. Maybe -- do you have the English version of the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: There is no German version of the statement, Your Honour. The original language that this statement was taken in is the English language with the assistance of the German interpreter, so the statement which would bear the signature of the witness is the English version. It's my belief that, as well, a B/C/S version was disclosed to the Defence, as was the case with all the other witness statements in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: My question is that -- do you have the English version at your hand?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I have a clean copy of it, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we also have the English version, but the witness does not speak English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we could give it to the witness and to the interpreter. At least the witness could see his signature or if there is --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can provide to the usher a clean copy of the statement of April 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let me put another question to you before that: Did you have some kind of a base in Doljani? Did you build a kind of a base there?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything of a construction that we would have constructed, or I would have constructed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Convicts Battalion in Doljani, did you build a base there?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing is known to me that I or that we would have built something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The houses that you pointed out on these photographs, you said that they were your base.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Interpreter, could you please look at the witness statement. 06 are the last two numbers on the top of the page. The number starts with 700, and then you will see 7006. These are the OTP numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't see --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the top of the page, in the middle. On the top of the page. And now, just go on until you get to the page where the last two numbers are "06."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: These pages are numbered 11 through 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a difference between the English and the Serbo-Croatian version. At the top of the page, you have a number. Would you please look at that. Find the page with the last two digits 06. You started from 700. Then it comes 701, 702, and we need 706.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You should check whether those are the same documents or not. I have some doubts about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. The English version has different numbering.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Counsel, I believe, is referring to what we call an ERN number, which is sort of a number that goes on to every piece of paper in the Office of the Prosecutor for reference purposes. When a document is translated, the translation is given a new ERN number, so the ERN number of the English version will not be the same as the ERN number for the B/C/S version. But I can inform Mr. Krsnik and also the Trial Chamber that I believe all versions will have a simple page number at the bottom which might assist in directing the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, my learned friend. Yes, I've found it, and now I realise it's page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So the first, second, third, fourth passage beginning the words "At the outset, it was a regular military operation ..." Did you find that? "A soldier was hit in the head when we were about to attack bunkers." "Hit in the head when we were about to attack bunkers." Then the next sentence: "We returned to the base which we had built in Doljani." Will you now please turn the page. First, second, third, fourth passage, and look for the text, then: "The Muslim people" -- "The Muslims, and only the Muslims, were expelled beyond the village limits. Those were people from the mosque -- those were the people from the mosque and one woman who was still in her house. Then they blew up the mosque. The mosque was near our headquarters in Doljani, and Tuta was present during this action."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Madam Interpreter, could we go back to the previous page, please. Will you now read one, two, three of the passages, and I will try to sum it up. It describes the event when the prisoners arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You described it to us, sir, the event with the prisoners. Do you remember that? Except that there is a big difference. Let's go back again to the next page, page number 8. You will find a sentence which reads, second passage from the bottom -- there is one sentence there, last sentence where you describe everything that happened in Doljani with the prisoners, the mosque, and the rest. And then you say: "After that, we went back to Siroki Brijeg to bury Cikota." And nowhere else do you mention in this statement that you returned after Cikota's funeral, and that it was then that the incident with the prisoners that you described yesterday happened. So my question is: Were you telling the truth when you described this incident?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say the following on that: And I always told the investigators -- it may happen that I get mixed up in -- with one operation or another operation, because it is not possible for me to remember exactly the dates or events - I'm sorry - and I constantly repeated it to the investigating bodies. It may happen time and again that I get mixed up, and I cannot -- and I just cannot remember dates exactly. And you can also ask the investigators that I constantly reminded them of this fact or deficiency of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, which of your statements is true? Yesterday, you said that you went for an operation in Doljani, Cikota was killed, you cut the action short, and two or three days later -- two or three days later, you came back to avenge Cikota's death, and then this scene with prisoners happened that you described to us. In this statement -- in your statement which you gave to the investigators of -- from The Hague, you say -- you give a completely different version. So I'm asking you which one of them is true, the one that you told yesterday to the Court or the one that you gave to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in Doljani twice or three times. After Cikota's death, we returned back to Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So what you say in this statement is not true?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may happen that things have been forgotten or somehow mixed up. I do not know. I cannot tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, could I have the English version of the 28th of October, 1998?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Simang, this statement was read out to you, you understood it, and you confirmed its authenticity with your signature. Now, I will show you the statement which you gave on the 28th of October, 1998, in the presence of Jan Van Hecke, Vassily Poriouvaev, and Harald Reiser, who is your lawyer. Will you please turn to page 4? One, two, three -- the third passage: "The cleansing of Doljani 1993 was performed under Tuta's command." Did you find that?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, you can read, and Madam Interpreter will help you. You describe here how you entered Doljani. Is that correct, that you drove in in cars -- no, sorry, that you met in Doljani, that you split into groups of five or six men each?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, which passage should I translate?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I merely wanted to quickly go through it. It starts with the sentence: "The cleansing of Doljani in April 1993." Madam Interpreter, I'm sorry, did we reach the place "A group of 15 soldiers was ordered to capture a bunker at the end of Doljani in the direction of Konjic-Jablanica"? Then the next sentence after that is: "There, Cikota died." And now the next passage -- and I'll read it aloud and you can check it with me: "There was a transport of Muslim prisoners of war from Doljani. The International Committee of the Red Cross turned up all of a sudden and stayed for ten minutes. Seven prisoners, and they were prisoners of war, were transported to Ljubuski in a Volkswagen van, escorted by soldiers." Now, the next sentence: "Before this transport, these prisoners were interrogated by Tuta and Andabak in a wooden cabin. We heard them cry out and scream during the interrogation, and we also heard the sound of blows. I also heard Tuta and Andabak yelling. Some of the prisoners were bleeding when they came out of the cabin. I do not remember any of the prisoners with firearm injuries."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, this is the third version. There is no execution by firing squad in this version. These prisoners, the same number, are taken to Ljubuski. Cikota was killed here in -- during the action. You did not return at all. And yesterday, you said that UNPROFOR arrived; here you say the International Committee of the Red Cross. You also confirmed the statement and confirmed its veracity with your signature. So now we have the third account of all these events. Is the statement correct?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct, and I can only repeat: Please do not put each word at its face value, because I -- what is written here is correct, but I cannot give you all the details in the -- in its sequence as they happened when they -- in those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, we are talking about one incident and one incident only. I am merely drawing your attention to the statements that you made before this Honourable Court and third statement that you gave to the investigators and prosecutors of the Tribunal. My question to you is: Are all these statements truthful? Because you confirm their veracity with your signature.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: The events are correct, but we were twice or three times at Doljani, as I mentioned yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Now, do you remember the statement that you gave to the German police on the 9th of October, 1995?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I could not tell when and what I should have said Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. there, because we are getting even back into earlier days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, I do not have that statement in English, but I shall be very brief, because I intend to tender this statement of yours into evidence. Oh, yes, we do have it in English.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to mention - I hope you also put it in as evidence - that I have withdrawn all statements from the German authorities. I hope you also have this in your records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it would assist the interpreter, I have that statement from the German proceedings which is in the German language, which I can offer to either counsel or the interpreter, if it would assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may furnish this to the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please look at page 2. Here, you offer a sixth version of the same event. But read it, first. I'll wait until you read it.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you want me to find?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: To read the second page. You describe there how you arrived in Doljani and how you started for the bunkers.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see anything here on page 2 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I meant -- or in German. Witness, will you please concentrate. German version; that is your mother tongue. And it says: "Everybody fired including myself"?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, on this second page, there is -- everything is written about this lady Elsa from South Africa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe that's a different version.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may well be. At least there's nothing written about Doljani, what I have got here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please, please. I'm sorry. Will you please find the text in German which begins with the words "Our unit had to retreat, as this was its responsibility. We took up our position during the night. And we started our action at about 0600. There were four bunkers that we were to take."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: May I help as an interpreter? It's page 3 on this paper of the 12th of October, 1995. Page 3, [German spoken], it starts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: That's the one.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I have got here is a statement made on the 5th of August, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe the usher will check the different versions, because here we are talking about a statement made on the 9th of October, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That's the Memmingen Court, on the 12th of October, 1995. That's true, but the statement itself was made on the 5th of August, 1994. What we have got as 12th of October, 1995, is the post stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, it seems to me there is great confusion here. Maybe someone could clear it up for us. Because we don't have all those statements at our hands, we cannot distinguish which one is which.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If I can inform counsel, if he turns to the top, page 2 of the English translation, the top of page 2 states: "Date of interview, 5th of August, 1994." The cover sheet appearing -- which is page 1 -- does contain the date of October 1995, but if counsel examined the document more closely, he would find the date of interview being, as indicated, 5th of August, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the interpreters have clarified it all and said so. The important thing for me is to find this passage, which does exist in this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Does this passage exist?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means -- so our unit had to move out; is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I have been asking you from the beginning to read the passage which begins with that sentence, and the whole page. And after that, I will ask you questions. This is the fourth time I'm asking you to do that.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Our unit had to move out" --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me. Please, sir, I wanted you to read it to yourself so that we don't waste any time. After that, I'll ask a question. If you want to read it aloud, then you can do that. I couldn't care less. I'm only having in mind the Honourable Court. Have you finished reading it?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Briefly, you say that it happened in May 1993, that you first took the bunkers. And then two weeks later, you had to make an assault on two more bunkers, and about 30 men stayed behind in the village, and I was one of them. So you did not leave the village? Then seven or eight Muslims were captured. And after the capture of those Muslims, you were informed by radio that Cikota had been killed. You were not with him at all. And on page 4, you end by saying, page 4, the first sentence: "We returned. As is usual when the commander dies, then the operation is discontinued and the unit goes back to bury him." And did you speak the truth on that occasion when you spoke to the German police?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned that all my statements which I have made in Germany with the police, that they were officially withdrawn in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So if the statement was withdrawn and it is no longer valid -- if the statement was withdrawn, as the witness says, does it mean that it is no longer valid?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. That's how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So it doesn't matter what it says here and what you said here?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: My statement with the police have been completely withdrawn and have been declared null and void.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And my question to you is: Is it truthful or did you lie, but to the German police, on that particular occasion?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may well be that I did not say everything there or that I concealed some facts and did not make a statement on other aspects.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But did you speak the truth? Excuse me, this is the last time I'm asking you that.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not with the police on several occasions, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you did not tell the truth to the police?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. That's what I just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Now tell me, on page 4 of that same statement, did you lie again when you said -- and you are describing the event in front of the ministry, remember that, the ministry in Mostar that you went with prisoners. And that is the passage one, two, three, fourth? Read it first.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not state the truth in some matters. I stated the truth in other matters. And this is why I withdrew my statement. And I'm going to repeat it now: You may read any of these sentences. Whatever you read out, I just comment on that that I have withdrawn completely my statement to the police. Sorry to say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, with all due respect to your comments, but I should like to verify one sentence. Will you please read it and see if you can confirm it? And it begins with the words "Tuta and Andabak came to interrogate the prisoners." The first, second, third, fourth passage. So the event in front of the Ministry of Defence in Mostar, then you go on: "Maximilian (surname, Resch) and I and another Croat called Branko stood outside by our truck with the Bofors." Have you found that? Read it.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not yet. Just hang on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Page 4. And then it says that you, Maximilian, and Branko were standing there. Have you found it? "Next to our truck with the Bofors. About 300 metres away." And that's the end of the sentence. Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: "We could not hear exactly what they were saying. Suddenly Tuta screamed at a prisoner, pulled out a pistol, held it to his head and pulled the trigger," et cetera. And then the next sentence: "The others were taken away. I do not know where." "The others" refers to the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: "Tuta and Andabak again drove off." And then you continue by saying: "In clarification, I state that Ivan Andabak also shot a prisoner dead in the head." And then you continue: "About an hour later we came with the other Croats who were standing around the Muslims talking. We asked them what was going on, and they said that the two dead men were wearing army shoes."

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So three things: Before this Court, you said that you -- I mean when this event in front of the ministry occurred, that you were in the immediate vicinity. Here you say that you were 300 metres away. Here you do not speak about the events that you described before this Court at all. You say that Tuta and Andabak left, and that you found out about all of this an hour later when you returned and when you talked to the soldiers. Here you say that they had army shoes, and then you also said before this Court that they had the imprint of a shell on their hands. Is that not true, then, what you said to the German police?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated several times it may well be that I did not state Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. everything -- did not say everything completely to the police and maybe that I also was mixed up. And by the way, the police did not ask me exactly for certain events. I just kept on rambling and talking and talking to the police. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, yesterday you talked and talked and talked, and I'm just checking about all these things that you talked about and what is true out of all the things that you have been talking about. Tell me, please, you have this statement of the 16th and 17th of April, 1997, the one that you gave to Jan Van Hecke, and Susan Somers was present as well. Please turn to page 6. This is paragraph 3, and it says: "One way or the other, there were some Muslims left in a big high school in West Mostar. Two days later, we got into Mostar again. We imprisoned 14 Muslims. Tuta came together with Andabak." You always said "Anderbag." And he personally questioned these 14 persons. And then you described the event that occurred in front of the Ministry of Defence in Mostar. Yesterday, I asked you --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. I'll try to be a bit slower. I do apologise to the lady interpreter. And then in this section that we've just read out, he describes the event that we referred to a few minutes ago, the one in front of the Ministry. If you want, you can read it, and I'll wait. We've just started with that. It's just underneath the section that I just read out, so if you would just proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The paragraph here in my version says something else than counsel said, and I just can't find it. If you would give me one minute to find it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on page number 6, right up at the start. It was -- it's paragraph 2. It starts with the sentence "There was blood coming from the left ear ..." If I understood you correctly in German, I think that we have read out as much as I actually wanted us to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yesterday, I asked you whether you remember the names of the persons who were present during this incident before the Ministry of Defence. Here, you say: "Among the other members of our unit who were present there, there were Vlado, Drago, Anderbag, Tuta, Cikota, Cikota's brother Bruno, Jablanica, Ivan [Tuta's driver], Zdenko." Here you say in the next sentence: "I was, at the moment when Tuta shot at the man, about 6 metres away from Tuta." Now, tell me, is this correct or is it incorrect? Did you stay to the truth here, or did you not state the truth here?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may well happen that the metres may not be very correct. I cannot give you the exact metres. That is not quite clear. As far as the names are concerned, it may well be that they were present. I do not know. But since I said it in this statement, so it obviously has happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How did it happen, the way you described it here or the way you described it to the German police? How did it happen? Because we have two totally different statements.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you previously, the statement I made to the police can be completely forgotten. Please drop it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You did not lie here when you made this statement to Mr. Van Hecke, and to Susan Somers?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may well be that some facts are blurred, but I repeat, I can say what happened and where it happened. But when it happened and each individual operation, I'm not so sure. We have been so often in these various places, so I do not know for sure and exactly for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yesterday, you also stated that the celebration of General Andabak's rank was at the Restaurant Kitic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you please take the statement that you gave on the 28th of October, 1998 - you have it in front of you - when Vassily Poriouvaev was present, and also your own attorney, Mr. Harald Reiser. Page number 2, paragraph number one, two, three: "When Andabak was promoted general, this promotion was granted from Zagreb." Question number one: How come you know it was granted from Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what was said to me. As I say, this all refers to hearsay. I personally was not present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. And now, tell me, do you know -- do you know about the command structure and the chain of command in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the command of chain was, we had General Tuta, we had Andabak, and then we had the ATG people, Lija and Cikota, as long as he has lived, and Baja also was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That's what you said yesterday, too. So these are the only people you know from the chain of command; is that right? No one else?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And on that basis, you concluded that they are the most important people and that they are the ones who are in charge?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let me continue this sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Interpreter, we stopped at the promotion being granted from Zagreb. Now we proceed. "People from Zagreb had come to Siroki Brijeg to give Andabak his promotion."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were you present then? Were you present when these people from Zagreb were promoting Andabak?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was not present. I know it from hearsay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Susak also came, and there was a big celebration in Hotel Park. Now, tell me, what is correct? What you said here or what you said yesterday before the Honourable Trial Chamber? Which version is not true?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, both of them. The first -- first, he was promoted. And then in a smaller circle, the usual celebrations were held up there with Kitic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All right. Very well. [In English] One moment, please. [Interpretation] Excuse me, I would like to put a different question to you now. Yesterday you said before this Trial Chamber that you saw Mr. Praljak only once, at a funeral at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Obviously the transcript rules, but I think that's not the witness's testimony from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, you may rephrase your question. I know what you are aiming at.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. My learned friend is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Once at the funeral and once at Mostar; that's what you said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I do apologise once again, indeed. This was not my intention. You have in front of you the statement you made on the 26th of August, 1999. Vassily Poriouvaev was present, Jan Van Hecke, and Harald Reiser, your attorney, were present.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Madam Interpreter -- oh, I do apologise. Have you read this section: "During the first attack in Rastani, I saw General Praljak"?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: "This was soon after the attack on Mostar. I would describe it in the following way. He had grey hair behind his ears. He had grey hair behind his ears. He was shorter than me, fat and plump. Plump." Tell me, please, how tall are you?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately 1 metre 75.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what you said here is true; right? It is true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe some things were mixed up, may well be. I'm sorry, but I stressed several times over, maybe certain things have been mixed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please look at this statement. You have the original version in the English language. Did you sign it and thus confirm its accuracy?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Or did you lie here as well? Had you ever seen Praljak? You would have remembered him because he's two metres tall.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said over and over again: First of all, these people were seated in the restaurant. This, second, in each statement, I usually referred to what I'm being asked at that moment, and I thought about things later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please, please. I am asking you about this statement. You're talking about Rastani. This is not at the restaurant. You're talking about the village of Rastani, and you say decidedly at Rastani you saw General Praljak and you give a description of him.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is mixed up. That was not Rastani, but this occurred to me only later, and I corrected it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Where did you correct it and how? When did you realise that? What is it that you have been correcting and where and when?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: In one of the later statements, I did not say Rastani. I then kept on saying Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, this is the last statement you gave to the Prosecution, on the 26th of August, 1999. Fortunately, we can check out these statements, because the names are here: Mr. Poriouvaev, Bridin O'Rourke, Jan Van Hecke, your lawyer Harald Reiser. Do you remember that this is your last statement? So you didn't say the truth even now? And can you tell me now whether you know where Sovici is? Have you ever heard of Sovici?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sovici?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You've never heard of the place?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sovici does not ring a bell with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And now tell me, yesterday we started talking about this. How did you reach Doljani? Via Jablanica or from Masna Luka?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Via Masna Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You've never heard of Sovici?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sovici does not ring a bell with me. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. All right. That's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, yes, we will resume at 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, were you in prison in 1993, any time in 1993?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was imprisoned for a short time at the border to Germany, and I was fined with a money fine, but that was paid later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I couldn't tell you the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But it was 1993, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this may well be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In the statement to the German police which you then withdrew, you said that you were released on the 12th of June, 1993. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not know. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, after that prison, when did you go back to Mostar in 1993 -- sorry, no. When did you go back to Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think immediately afterwards, but I do not know which month and day it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In that same statement, the one that you gave to the German police, you say that you returned sometime before the 20th of June, 1993, and it was then that Mr. Heinz was murdered, for which then you were sentenced. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: This may well be, but I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Then in your statement, you also said - and you have it - that there were no actions from the month of June onward. And it is the last page of your statement, the very beginning of it. You say: "Later on, that is, until the 20th of August, 1993, we took part in two or three actions, but nothing happened during them."

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned previously that this entire statement - and I think we had agreed on that - that I did not mention all details, that I intentionally skipped a few matters and intentionally did not say the truth in some parts and that I officially then withdrew this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I apologise. Yes, I heard your answer. Never mind. And finally, as regard to this statement, you also withdrew the sentence which is on the first page of that text: "I swear by God and Elsa's life (I swear by Elsa's life because this is the most valuable thing and the most dearest thing to me) that I shall never again wrong anyone ever. So will you please do all within your power so that I am not separated from my happiness for much longer." Did you withdraw that, too; that is, not the last wrong that you did?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I withdrew my entire statement, all statements which I have made to the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very good. Tell me, I asked you yesterday if you knew that an investigation had been conducted against you, an investigation which you were the first accused and Mladen Naletilic the second accused, and which was conducted by the Federal Bureau for Criminal Investigation in Germany, and that you were suspected of having committed a war crime, that is, the genocide. I believe it says so. Do you-- are you aware of the investigation, that witnesses were interviewed, that you gave a statement in relation to that investigation?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, you did not tell me that Mr. Mladen Naletilic, General Tuta, was the second one. You didn't tell me that. I have only been informed that there was an investigation against me by the Federal authorities in Germany, and this investigation process was then cancelled against me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. And Will Roland Franz was one of the potential witnesses interviewed in that case. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: This name does not ring any bell with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: He's the man who took you to the programme called "Einspruch"?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only am aware of a person called Roland Will.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That's the person that I asked you about, Roland Will Franz. That is the person I just asked you about.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this man is known to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You travelled with that man from Siroki Brijeg to Germany, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are you on good terms with him?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know him from these few days where we had been on our way and where we were on this TV programme in Sat 1, "Einspruch."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In his statement to the Federal Bureau for Criminal Investigation as a witness, he said about you: "As for Falk Simang, the question of moral conscience, human rights and ethics were of no importance whatsoever."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I object. I think that the witness doesn't know about what other people have said in other statements. There is certainly nothing to prevent the Defence from calling people to testify, but I think that this manner or attempt of impeachment is improper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik, will you please skip this question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, may I answer my learned friend? I asked were they on any terms and what kind of terms, and I wanted to ask this witness if he knows why did this man state this. I merely asked him. I did not affirm -- I did not put it to him that he knew what this man had said about him, but possibly we shall bear in mind this possible witness and call him if necessary. But I was merely trying to see whether they were on good -- on good terms or not. But never mind. Let's avoid any further discussion. I withdraw my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Witness, what kind of a patch did you have on your uniform, on the sleeve of your uniform?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HVO sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And all the members of your unit had the same patch, did they?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this may well be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the ID that we saw yesterday says only that you are a member of the HVO and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when you returned from the prison in Germany, did you stop in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would not know any more. Maybe, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you run into any trouble with Mafia in Zagreb and you fled from them and hid in Siroki Brijeg? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, nothing of that sort is known to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are you aware that they looked for you in Siroki Brijeg and inquired about you, those men from Zagreb? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing is known to me about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: At the Heliodrom, where you spent a very short time, as you stated, could you tell the Court if it is a large facility, were there many troops there, or were you the only troops that were there?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, our unit was the only one. At least in the building where I was, we were the only unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was there a military prison there?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was something like that there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And there were soldiers there serving some disciplinary punishment or similar types of punishment?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may well be, but I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How do you know that General Praljak is a general in the Croatian army? Did somebody tell you that, or do you know it of your own knowledge? How did you arrive at that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, I was told that he was a general of the HV, and then he had a patch at his chest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: On his chest, you mean? Here? Here?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a patch indicating a rank, and nobody from our side used to have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And where did the HVO officers have their rank insignia?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, none of ours had such a rank. It was all on the Iskaznica. For instance, in the case of Mr. Mrachacz, it said "captain" in Croatian language, and that's all I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And they had no insignia whatsoever on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nothing is known to me that in our unit that somebody would have a rank insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And on the basis of what you saw, that Mr. Praljak had his rank insignia on his breast, you concluded from that that he was a general in the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, by no means. I do neither know the rank insignia of a general. I was just told that it was so. But I cannot tell you whether this was the rank insignia of a general.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And who told you that he was a general?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mrachacz told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please -- we shall first -- but very briefly, only a few questions to do with your statements, and then we shall be over and move on to a completely different subject. Tell me, please, you have the statement before you, 20th of August, '97. You have it? Page 5.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: 26 August 1999, or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: 20th of August. We already had a look at this statement. 20th of August, 1997, present Jan Van Hecke and Peter Nicholson.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: 16th, 17th of April I've got here, but I have no statement of the 20th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So far as I know, it is 1998, rather than 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, both on the English and the Croatian version, it says the 20th of August, 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is a statement dated the 20th of August, 1997. I don't know whether it has been provided to the witness yet. I do have an extra copy of it, if it would assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Certainly not, because we haven't been informed about this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could it be furnished to the witness, if you want to ask some questions about the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'll apologise. I must find that particular passage so as not to waste too much time. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Tell me, please, do you remember what you said before this Court yesterday about the action at high noon?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You said that morning Tuta had given you your tasks, and at high noon. Remember that?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, my colleagues are looking for the statement on page 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [In English] Please be so kind as to give the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I underlined the beginning of the passage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I just wasn't clear which statement we're working with now, the date of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My learned friend, the 20th of August, 1997. In the English version, it is page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And here you say as follows: "At 10.00, the order came to shell the minarets. The order was given by an officer, whose name I do not know, who arrived in a new BMW 3 series. He told us which minaret we were to fire at and also told us to wait. Then he drove further to other units." Do you remember giving that -- making the statement to the investigators of this Tribunal and confirming its authenticity with your signature?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: This may well be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, is this true? Did you lie in this statement, or did you lie before the Court yesterday? You said that that morning at a meeting, Tuta assigned the tasks and everything else and then called you at noon on his Motorola.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Both is true. In the morning, we were given orders. We were given a map. And on top of the hill where we were to take our position, this man with the BMW came on top of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Fine, fine. And to cap it all, where was your position with Bofors in Mostar? Where were you positioned in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean at this "high noon" mission? On a hill, on a slope so that we could shoot target at the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But I'm talking about only that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [In English] Exhibit Number 11.18.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you please take the pointer and show us where were you exactly. And this is a very good plan of Mostar with all the streets and even the surroundings.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I can't recognise anything on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Will you, then, take your statement of the 16th and 17th of April, 1997. You have it before you. It's the one when Jan Van Hecke and Susan Somers were present. Last page, last passage. It's the last passage, and it says: "I remember one more incident when Tuta ordered to shell the mosque in East Mostar on a day in September 1993 at 12.00. That morning, Tuta briefed us and we had to go to our positions. The coordinates of the mosque were given to the artillery, and at exactly 12.00 noon Tuta ordered to start -- to issue the order over Motorola to start the shelling." And now I skip the following two or three sentences, and I'm coming to the last two or three sentences or, rather, the last sentence in your statement -- no, the last two sentences are: "My position was on the hill above the Mostar hospital, about 2.5 metres away from my target."

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Over here it says 2 and a half metres in my statement.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my version, it says kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All right. This can be checked. In my version, it says 2 and a half metres. Has this jogged your memory? Do you remember where your position was now? Can you point out the hill above Mostar and also where your target was?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry, I cannot point at that. I'm not well-versed at all with maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You don't even know how far the hospital in Mostar was -- is from the eastern part or, rather, the hill above the hospital?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So then this officer who came to see you at 10.00, he was not there?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot even say whether there were hills. The only thing I know is that we had maps, that we were given orders, what we had to fire at. But I cannot tell you where exactly our position was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So what it says here, that you were on a hill above the Mostar hospital, is simply not true?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wouldn't say that. It may well be true, but I'm sorry, I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And where was your target? What was your target? You said that you knew exactly what your target was and that it was two and a half kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: My objection, Mr. President, is that counsel has just given the witness two questions, neither of which he's allowed the witness to answer. I'm just simply asking the witness be allowed to answer the two questions: "Where was your target? What was your target?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could I please have answers to these questions?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our target was on the Muslim side. Eastern or western side, I always get mixed up. It was to shoot over the Neretva --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And could the witness please repeat the last words?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the other side of the Neretva. We were to target at mosques, at minarets. We had a map, and there it was exactly given and drawn in what we should have to fire at.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. And my final question related to your statements. Please this last statement I gave you, the 20th of August, 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, Madam Interpreter, that it's somewhere around page number 5. I think we've underlined it in the version that you have. I think that my colleagues marked this passage. "The other day" -- THE ENGLISH INTERPRETER: Could the counsel please slow down? The booth is unable to follow him. THE GERMAN INTERPRETER: I'm sorry, what is underlined is on page 6. It says: "At 10.00 the order came to shell the minarets." That's what's underneath this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, it's either page number 4 or page number 5. I really don't know. I gave it to my colleagues so that they could check it out. [In English] Oh, you have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is precisely the passage I was referring to. I'm going to read these two sentences for the Trial Chamber. "The other day of the operation Tuta said we had to cleanse the other part of Mostar --" THE ENGLISH INTERPRETER: This is too fast for the booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The eastern part was supposed to be separated from the western part. This order was issued to us in the Croatian language. Vlado translated it for us. Andabak was present, at the time a colonel, as well as Cikota, who was either a major or a lieutenant colonel. Leia [as interpreted] and Baja were also present together with the whole ATG." Is that correct? That statement, is it correct?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may well be. I do not know. I do not even know which operation is meant here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, you've just read it twice. "The other day of the operation, Tuta said that we had to cleanse the western side of Mostar."

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this has nothing to do with the 12 "high noon" operation. This must be something else here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Of course it's something else. Of course it is. That's why I gave you this to read. Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I think you have to be fair to this witness. You should concentrate on one statement, then another, rather than moving from one statement to another at the same time. And also you 8 have to organise your cross-examination, for one part just mainly dealing with the statements, for the other part just to deal with the other facts. It is very difficult, even for us, to follow you all the way down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I just concluded with the statements, and now I'm moving on to the other part of my cross-examination. However, I did give this to the witness to read, and it says here clearly, quite clearly, absolutely clearly what this is. It is an order that was issued. And I asked whether that is correct and whether these people actually were present. It's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, he has to have an opportunity to realise from which statement that particular paragraph has come. He has to have an opportunity to see it in context, because I can tell you, Mr. Krsnik, I am utterly confused in relation to the statements. And I think I speak for the Bench. We would like an opportunity to see these statements. I don't know what particular passage you are putting to the witness. For instance, the witness was answering the 12 -- the "high noon" operation, and then we talk about a number of senior officers who were present with no relationship between which operation you are talking about. And you have to be fair to him. He seems to have made a lot of statements. It isn't fair, in my view, for you to take a small part of a statement out of context. So I know what you are trying to do, and you are doing it very well, but you really must be more fair to him and maybe to the Bench as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I personally wanted to add that since we have in front of us a witness who is very willing to cooperate so far, there is no point in repeating that you've lied or have you lied again, since he, himself, recognises that. He said he hasn't told the whole truth. He withdrew it all. Because if he stops cooperating, we won't be served by that at all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, for everything you have cautioned me about. I shall certainly abide by that. But we are doing all of this for you, and it is the most important thing for you to be able to follow all of this. I'm so sorry there has been a misunderstanding. I seem to have things in my head, and then I keep forgetting that other people do not.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel will have to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seem to think that everybody has all of this in their minds, and then I keep rushing matters. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So this last section that we had discussed; that is, the statement that you gave on the 20th of August, 1997. Present were Jan Van Hecke and Peter Nicholson. Lothar Wogschin was the interpreter. And it concerns a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. particular action in Mostar which has nothing in common with the action that you called the "high noon" action, either in terms of time or in terms of anything else. This particular action is the one that you have just read out to us; that is, that Tuta issued you an order to cleanse the western part of Mostar. I think that's what you read out. Right?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now we know what action we are talking about. Now we understand fully which action we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I honestly think that to be of assistance to us, that this witness should be given an opportunity to read his entire statement, not just a piece of it, and that takes a little time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. It is precisely because of time that I did not suggest that. But by all means, let him read the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: THE WITNESS'S INTERPRETER: There's an abbreviation in the statement, "JNA." This is on page 3, fourth paragraph, and the witness does not know what this abbreviation means. I think most of the other soldiers in KB had served in the JNA. THE ENGLISH INTERPRETER: Interpretation booth notes that JNA is Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be of assistance, this is the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We agree. [Statement read to witness].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: While the witness is reading the statement, could I ask Mr. Stringer to do something for us?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The first thing is that could we be furnished with all those statements? So far as I know, there are about six statements given by this witness before. And the second thing is that could you provide us some information concerning with the legal status of the statement given by this witness to the German police? He himself claimed that those witnesses officially withdraw. In some jurisdictions, the unilateral withdrawal is valid; in some others, it's not. We just want to know some background of the legal status of the statements given to the German police.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can inform the Trial Chamber there are four statements which the witness provided to the Office of the Prosecutor, and then the fifth is the earliest, which is the one that was provided to the German authorities, which you've heard about. During the course of the investigation, the Office of the Prosecutor obtained, from the German authorities, the Prosecution file, if you will, which was disclosed to the Defence during the pre-trial phase of this case. I don't know at this time the legal effect in Germany of withdrawing one's statement, but we can perhaps make that inquiry to the German government and provide that information to the Trial Chamber. We will provide all of those statements to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Krsnik? You want to add something on this very issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Your Honour, for giving me the floor. I think that I can be of assistance to the Trial Chamber because I am familiar with German law because our own system relies almost 90 per cent to criminal -- on criminal procedure as it is in Germany and Austria, with a few exceptions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You are also invited to submit your submissions concerning with this matter. We are not going to debate it in the courtroom at this moment. Mr. Stringer, we also would like to know the -- whether you could provide us with the statements of another convicted witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That would be the other prisoner that appeared before the Trial Chamber some weeks ago?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, we can provide all statements. I don't know if there is one that comes from the German proceedings, but whatever we have, we will provide to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, Your Honours, can I just ask the lady interpreter whether they have come to the section that I asked about? Because that is what matters. Afterwards, it deals with completely different things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask you, Madam Interpreter, have you reached the section that we had discussed before? THE WITNESS'S INTERPRETER: Your Honour, I read -- we read through the beginning of page 4 where it says "We had five or six targets." That is the third paragraph on page 4. That is the last one I translated for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to ask you to stop when you reach the section that I had been referring to, because after that, the statement deals with completely different matters. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Could I take the opportunity of asking either the Prosecution or the Defence, if either of you can assist us, to see whether on the map that was provided to us that we could find the village of Masna Luka? Because we have been singularly unsuccessful.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It is on there. If it's all right, I could point to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: If you give it to the usher, I will share it with the -- [no microphone].

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: With the Trial Chamber's permission, I could highlight that place. THE WITNESS'S INTERPRETER: The whole 18G is the last part I translated for the witness, on page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have read the whole statement now, and you, I guess, understand -- only down to the passage that we've already read out three times, and will you stop there, please, Madam Interpreter. THE WITNESS'S INTERPRETER: This is where I stopped, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All I want to ask you is: In that statement which you gave to the Prosecutor's Office and confirmed with your signature, now you've read it through, what the Defence would like to know, when that order was issued to separate the western from the eastern part of Mostar, that that order was issued and it was translated by Vlado or the present Andabak who at that time was a colonel, as well as Cikota, who had -- who was either a major or a lieutenant colonel -- now, my first question is: Is that true and is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may well be true. Unfortunately, I cannot remember the whole statement, and I do not know what it's all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: There are a number of -- there is a number of points that are found in those passages, and we'd ask the witness be directed specifically to a point. If counsel is challenging or wishes to put a specific point to the witness, he should do it. But there is an indication about Andabak being a colonel, a number of people present, Tuta issued the order to separate east from west. What is the point that he asks the witness to affirm or to deny? That's our request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, this is a statement made by this witness before. It is all there. There's no need to ask him whether it's truth or is it correct. You just need to ask another question, following question, rather than this one. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, we read the passage four times during the cross-examination. Now, we read the integral text. The first question that is of my concern, Your Honours, is whether the statement which we've read is true and correct. Now, my second question will come, and my second question is: How does he know that Andabak was a colonel?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
